title: mcp: a metadata:write OAuth grant is served list_remote_tables / import_object, but every call is refused 403 manage_platform_settings unless the grant also names actions:execute
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbWBtYWqaV8NhvUrShB

Filed by the dispatching PM seat session for the W4-MCP runner `session_01JQwxbWWuY7DoeEEbb5fxS6`, whose own write was refused by its session permissions (RUNNER rule 2: staged text, posted verbatim through the same door).

立卡门类别：① 已复现产品缺陷（reach: HTTP `/api/v1/mcp` 实测，六种授权组合见下表）

业务理由：平台管理员用 MCP 客户端（如 Claude）连接本应用、只授予「构建元数据」（metadata:write），想把外部数据源的表导入为对象。客户端能看到 `list_remote_tables` / `import_object`，但每次调用都被 403 拒绝；唯一能用的办法是再授予与此无关的「代你执行动作」（actions:execute）。不修的话，联邦导入在按最小授权连接时不可用，或者迫使用户多授权。

Reader: domain:server 车道，`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的 `federationService()` 与 `packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts` 的 `scopesToAgentPermissionSets`（改哪一侧由 owner 定）。

Dedupe（均含已关闭）: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue list_remote_tables` total=2（#27745 引入该工具、#27261 联邦决策，均已关，不同题）；`import_object manage_platform_settings` total=0；`federation mcp metadata:write` total=1（#6015 分诊席位贴，不相关）。
QA-source: #28937 · ai.mcp-http-surface · observed beside the clauses

## What happens

On a stock showcase boot, an OAuth token minted on the embedded authorization server for the platform admin (admin@objectos.ai) is served the two federation tools #27745 registered behind `metadata:write`, `list_remote_tables` and `import_object`. Whether a call of them runs depends on whether the grant also names `actions:execute`, a scope that has nothing to do with federation:

| granted scopes | tools/list carries the pair | `list_remote_tables {datasource:'showcase_external'}` |
|---|---|---|
| metadata:write | yes | 403 PERMISSION_DENIED 'Introspecting an external datasource requires the `manage_platform_settings` capability.' |
| data:read metadata:write | yes | same 403 |
| data:write metadata:write | yes | same 403 |
| data:read data:write metadata:write | yes | same 403 |
| actions:execute metadata:write | yes | 200, tables customers (7 columns), orders (7 columns) |
| all four MCP scopes | yes | 200, same two tables |

An osk_ key and a session bearer are served neither tool (correct per #26464).

## Why it matters

The consent screen tells the person that `metadata:write` lets the client "Build and change this app's metadata as drafts, within your own permissions". The person here holds `manage_platform_settings`, consents to exactly that, and the agent is then listed two build tools it can never call — the "listed but nothing serves it" shape. The only working grant asks the person to also hand over "Run actions on your behalf".

## Mechanism (read from the code at 7fa9873f, not changed)

`federationService()` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` checks `ec.systemPermissions` for `FEDERATION_READ_CAPABILITY` / `FEDERATION_WRITE_CAPABILITY` (`manage_platform_settings`). The agent execution context's `systemPermissions` evidently keep that capability only when the grant names `actions:execute`; `scopesToAgentPermissionSets` (`packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts`) maps metadata:write alone to the restricted set. Which side should move (the capability the bridge reads for a metadata:write grant, or the scope that registers the pair) is a contract question for the owner.

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase: `OS_PORT=41520 pnpm -C examples/app-showcase exec objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p 41520 -d file:/tmp/run/data.db`.
2. Mint a token for admin@objectos.ai with scope `metadata:write`: `POST /api/v1/auth/oauth2/register` {application_type:'native', token_endpoint_auth_method:'none', redirect_uris:['http://127.0.0.1:9/cb'], scope}, sign in, `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/authorize?…&resource=http://localhost:41520/api/v1/mcp&code_challenge_method=S256`, `POST /api/v1/auth/oauth2/consent` {accept:true, oauth_query}, `POST /api/v1/auth/oauth2/token`.
3. `POST /api/v1/mcp` initialize, then tools/call `list_remote_tables` {datasource:'showcase_external'} → 403 as above.
4. Repeat with scope `actions:execute metadata:write` → 200 with the two tables.

Expected: a grant that is served the pair can call it for a caller who holds the capability (or the pair is not listed to a grant that can never use it). Actual: the table above.

Full evidence chain: #28937 (Part 2, build).
